sentences.text: : JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 31.10.2020 at about 1.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding his scooter bearing No.KA-05-AJ-8801 and while taking 'U' turn at Veerasandra junction, Hosur main road, Electronic City, Bengaluru, at that time, tempo bearing No.KA-59-1916 driven by its driver came at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Kaveri hospital,
Bengaluru for first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Jyotsna hospital for treatment wherein he was treated as an inpatient.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as car AC mechanic and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

4. It is further case of the petitioner that the Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the tempo are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

Hence, this Petition.
5.
In response to the notice, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the court through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statement to the main petition.
Respondent No.1 in his Written Statement he denies negligent driving of tempo by its driver.
He further contended that the tempo is insured with the respondent No.2 and it was valid at the time of accident.
The driver of the Tempo had driving licence to drive the vehicle.
He further contended that the rider of the scooter rode in rash and negligence manner and hit the Tempo and cased the accident.
He denied the income of the petitioner and expenses incurred for the treatment.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

In the objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the tempo.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.

Further, it contended that, the accident occurred due Syed Shadab vs Tavera Mines And Minerals on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198249225/
2 to the negligence of the petitioner being the rider of motor cycle and he had no valid driving licence to ride the said vehicle.

sentences.text: Further it contended that owner of the insured tempo has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 31.10.2020 at about 1.00 p.m. Veerasandra junction, Hosur main road, Electronic City, Bengaluru, in an accident arising due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of tempo bearing No.KA-59-1916?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.14.
He got examined two witnesses as PW.2 and 3 and got marked Ex.P.15 to 18 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 got examined its officer as as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3.
Respondent No.1 has not chosen to lead evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and Respondent No.2 and on perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 9. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 31.10.2020 at about 1.00 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-59-1916 by its driver.
10. On the other hand, the Respondents have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-59-1916 by its driver.

11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked Syed Shadab vs Tavera Mines And Minerals on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198249225/
3 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-14.

sentences.text: He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.
Ex.P-1 to 4 and 11 are the true copies of FIR along with complaint, spot mahazar along with spot sketch, IMV report, charge sheet and Wound Certificate.

Ex.P.5 and 12 are the discharge summaries,
Ex.P.6 and 13 are Medical bills, Ex.P.7 and 14 are Medical Prescriptions, Ex.P.8 is the medical reports, Ex.P.9 is the notarized copy of aadhar card, Ex.P.10 is the X-rays.

12. Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR along with complaint, it justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Electronic City Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of tempo bearing Regn.No.KA-59-1916 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar and spot sketch drawn in the presence of panchas.
They show that the road where accident has occurred was two ways and each road contains 3 lanes and there was median also.
Wherein, exact place of accident is shown.
As per this sketch while the petitioner was taking 'U' turn, the offending Tempo which coming from his back side had hit the bike.
It makes it clear that the accident has occurred due to negligent driving the offending Tempo.

Ex.P.3 is the IMV report which shows that accident is not caused due to any mechanical defects and the damages found on both vehicle justify the fact of involvement of vehicles in question in the accident.

The Ex.P.4 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Electronic City Police Station has Charge-sheeted the driver of the offending tempo for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
The document Ex.P.11 is the wound certificate which shows that petitioner has sustained simple injuries.
13. During cross examination of petitioner by learned advocate for respondent No.2, he admitted that the vehicle which he was riding belongs to Ogo Company.
He had admitted that to book Ogo vehicle driving licence is must.
He admitted that the tempo was coming from his bike.
He was riding on the right side of the road.
His vehicle got damaged front side towards left.
He admitted that there was signal at the time of accident.
He denied the suggestion that the accident took place due to his negligence.
14. He further admitted that he rushed to Kaveri Hospital after the accident.
Wherein he was treated for 2-3 hours.
He left home and then went to Jyotsna Hospital as he was told that the cost of treatment would be expensive in the Kavery hospital.
He further admitted that in the Kaveri hospital they told him that his left ankle was fractured.
He has admitted that after 7 days of the accident he was admitted to Jyotsna hospital.
15. Further, the petitioner got examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N. as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.15 and 16 i.e., clinical notes and X-ray.
In his examination in chief he deposed about the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by him.
Further he assessed the disability.
During his cross examination, he admits that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has admitted that as per Ex.P.17 all the injuries are simple in nature and he voluntaries that injury no.1 shows quiry but no further investigation was done at the point of time.
He has further admitted that as per the recent X-ray the fractures are united with implants in situ.
He has also admitted that the complaints mentioned in para no.5 does not arise in young person.
He has admitted that there is no injury to the knee.

Further, the petitioner got examined Dr.Vinay.H.N as PW.3 and got marked Ex.P.17 and 18 i.e.,
wound certificate and MLC register.
He has deposed that petitioner had come directly to their hospital for treatment.
He has admitted that there is no mention of vehicle number in Ex.P.18.
He admitted that in the Ex.P.17 it is mentioned that the injuries are simple in nature.
17. The respondent No.2 got examined his officer as RW.1.
In his examination in chief he reiterated the averments of the written statement.
He got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 i.e., copy of policy with conditions, letter to insured with acknowledgment and letter to driver with postal receipt.
18. During cross examination by learned advocate for petitioner, he admits that the said vehicle has been issued policy from their company and the charge sheet is filed against the driver of tempo.
He has admitted that police have received information that the driver had DL.
He also admits that the charge sheet is is not filed for not having DL.
19. Learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 vehemently argued that the wound certificate issued by the Kavery hospital shows that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are simple in nature.
Hence, it should be considered.
A careful perusal of Ex.P.11 wound certificate issued by Kavery hospital, it shows that the injuries are simple in nature.
Wherein it is mentioned that investigation was not done.
Therefore, it is clear that without investigation they mentioned that the injuries are simple in nature.
Obviously without investigation it can not be opined that injuries are grievous in nature.
As per the petitioner he was stayed in the Kavery hospital only for 2-3 hours and he got discharged as the cost of treatment would be expensive there.
Thereafter he was shifted to Jyotsna hospital for further treatment, wherein surgery was done to the both bone and implants were fixed.
The Ex.P.5 discharge summary shows that the petitioner was sustained type 2 open comminited fracture of both bones left leg.
Even the PW.2 doctor who assessed the disability also clearly deposed about the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the treatment taken by him.
The IO had taken the wound certificate where only first aid treatment was given.
The IO ought have taken wound certificate from the hospital where complete treatment was given.

Therefore though in the wound certificate it is mentioned that the injuries are simple in nature, but the other medical records made it clear that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.
Hence this tribunal is considered opine that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not the simple in nature and they are grievous in nature.

20. Next coming to the negligent aspect, the charge sheet is the material document which is filed against the driver of the offending Tempo has not been challenged by its driver and the Respondent No.1 who is the owner of the said vehicle appeared before this Tribunal and filed his objection statement, wherein he has not denied the involvement of the vehicle.
But he only formally denied the rash and negligent driving of the said vehicle.
The Respondents though they denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending tempo, nothing elicited from the mouth of petitioner to prove their contention.
Even they have not bothered to examine the driver of the offending vehicle to prove their contention.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tempo in the said accident,
the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

sentences.text: Issue No. 2 :

As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending tempo by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
22.
In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 19 years.
He has produced Ex.P.9, aadhar card to prove his age.
As per aadhar card, his date of birth is shown as 21.02.2001.
The accident has taken place on 31.10.2020.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 19 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
23. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as AC mechanic and was earning of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any evidence to prove his income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.14,500/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2020, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
24. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
 I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
25.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.11

Wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries:
1. Laceration 2cm x 2cm present over lower 3rd of left leg with deformity (? fracture )
investigations not done.
2. Abrasions present on left eyebrow 1 cmx 1cm.
3. Abrasion 3 cmx 2cms present over left knee 4. Abrasion 2 cms x 2cms over medial aspect of left ankle.
5. Punctured wound present on the left ankle with bleeding.
The doctor has opined that injury No.1 to 5 are simple in nature.
As per wound certificate issued by Kavery hospital, the injuries are simple in nature.
Whereas, in the discharge summary of Jyotsnareddy hospital it is mentioned that type 2 open communited fracture of both bones left leg.
Even the PW.2 doctor as reiterated the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
As discussed above the oral and medical record show that the injuries sustained by the petitioner are grievous in nature.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
II
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :

sentences.text: Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
27.
The Petitioner has averred that he was treated as an inpatient in the Jyotsna hospital.

Further,
P.W.2 Dr.Nagaraj.B.N has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
The Ex.P.5 discharge summary shows that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient in Jyotsna hospital on 06.11.2020 and discharged on 13.11.2023.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 7 days.
28. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.29,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,500/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
29.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
30. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 28 medical bills i.e., Ex.P6 amounting to Rs.1,24,502/-.
He has also produced 20 medical bills i.e., Ex.P13 amounting to Rs.13,547/- which is totally amounting to Rs.1,38,049/-.
There is no dispute about the medical bills.
Hence, the same are accepted.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,38,100/- as a compensation under this head.

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
31.

The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has Syed Shadab vs Tavera Mines And Minerals on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198249225/
7 suffered permanent disablement and he was not able to move or carry out any activities, not able to sleep properly, often get pain in his leg, there are ugly looking scars over his fracture site, there is restriction of movement s in his left, he cannot walk briskly, cannot stand for long duration, walk for long distance.

sentences.text:
Further, the petitioner got examined Dr.Nagaraj.B.N. as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.15 and 16 i.e.,
clinical notes and X- ray.
He assessed physical disability of the left lower limb at 42% and whole body at 14%.
During his cross examination, he admits that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has further admitted that as per the recent X-ray the fractures are united and implants are in situ.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 14% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the age of Petitioner is 18.

With multiplier of 18, income of Rs.14,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 14%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,38,400/- (Rs.14,500 x 12 x 18 x 14/100 =4,38,400/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,38,480/- under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs.1,38,100/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 29,000/-
laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.4,38,480/-

Total Rs.6,83,580/-

sentences.text: Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.6,83,580/- which is rounded off Rs.6,83,600/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending tempo bearing No.KA-59-1916.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
34. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner is entitled to Compensation of Rs.6,83,600/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, 75%
of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E- payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
